regions.label: MZ header
regions.note: DOS EXE header, rebuilt by the museum unpacker after removing the DIET compression.

regions.label: Relocation table
regions.note: 1,746 addresses that DOS patches at load time, mostly far calls between the code segments of a large-model program.

regions.label: Header padding
regions.note: Fills the header to a 16-byte boundary.

regions.label: Borland C++ startup (c0)
regions.note: Sets up memory, then calls main() far at 0302:0007 with far argv and envp, the sign of the large memory model.

regions.label: Borland C++ runtime library
regions.note: printf, farmalloc, bioskey, sin, cos and the start of the floating-point support.

regions.label: Help pop-up (segment 02DE)
regions.note: F1 from anywhere: saves the screen under a box with getimage, draws the key list, restores it with putimage.

regions.label: main() (segment 0302)
regions.note: Checks that ARABART is in memory, shows the opening verse, the title and the poem, then runs the menu through a table of five choices.

regions.label: The sun in the Quran (segment 030C)
regions.note: An illustrated introduction, then the fifteen verse cards, each laid out by hand.

regions.label: ARABART helpers (segment 04B6)
regions.note: Small C functions with a few lines of assembly inside that call ARABART through the video service, plus his shadow and outline effects.

regions.label: Screen kit (segment 04DA)
regions.note: Starting the graphics, his 16 colors, the opening verse, keys, panels and edges, the menu, the sun drawn in the dark and the closing card.

regions.label: Poem screen (segment 0629)
regions.note: His prose poem to the sun beside a night sky with a moon and clouds.

regions.label: The sun and nature (segment 06D2)
regions.note: The solar system with Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars moving at the pace of their years, then the sun’s facts, its mass and its density.

regions.label: Cycle of life (segment 082C)
regions.note: Nine pages: day and night, the seasons, the phases of the Moon and the water cycle, each with its own animation.

regions.label: Floating-point emulator
regions.note: Borland code that does the math chip’s work in software, for sine and cosine on PCs without one (about 10 KB).

regions.label: 8087 fix-up and error handler
regions.note: Turns the placeholders for math instructions into real ones when the PC has a math chip.

regions.label: BGI graphics library
regions.note: initgraph, line, putimage, setrgbpalette and the rest of Borland Graphics Interface; the driver itself loads from EGAVGA.BGI.

regions.label: Runtime data
regions.note: Borland copyright and the "Abnormal program termination" message.

regions.label: His texts and constants
regions.note: All the Arabic, typed as the English keys of an Arabic keyboard, and the numbers of the orbits: sizes in pixels and the planets’ years.

regions.label: Data
regions.note: Sixty-four bytes of data between his texts and the runtime data.

regions.label: Runtime and BGI data
regions.note: Floating-point error messages, math constants, BGI error strings and driver tables.

routines.name: main
routines.note: The ARABART check, the opening screens, then the menu loop.

lines.note: If not, print the error and leave
Back to DOS: mov ah,4Ch / int 21h

routines.name: ar_installed
routines.note: INT 10h with AX=3600h asks ARABART if it is there; it answers 5944h, and minus 5943h that makes 1.

lines.note: sub ax,5943h turns the answer into 1

routines.name: shadow_text
routines.note: Draws a line in dark color 8, 6 pixels down and right, then in its own color on top.

routines.name: outline_text
routines.note: Draws a string 4 times at the diagonal 1-pixel offsets, then once in the middle in a second color.

routines.name: draw_sun
routines.note: Six discs in 6 palette slots set to black, then the slots become six shades from (63,50,0) to (63,38,0).

routines.name: solar_system
routines.note: Draws the four planet pictures, then stamps them on their ovals every frame until a key is pressed.

lines.note: Earth: divided by its year, times 88
Loop while no key is waiting

routines.name: exit_screen
routines.note: The closing card with his name, a key, then back to text mode and DOS.
